body.x: On January 9th (local time), GhostPass, a specialized company in private biometric information security (CEO Seon Gwan Lee), unveiled a 'Decentralized, remote self-verification solution (tentatively named: Gpass)' at 'CES 2024' held in Las Vegas, USA. This solution allows easy authentication and payment using biometric information stored on smartphones.

GhostPass is a solution that enables more secure and convenient self-verification and payment using biometric information stored on one's smart device (smartphone). The company also conducts technology verification (PoC) with specialized smart home companies, security companies, etc.

In particular, GhostPass has adopted a decentralized system where users manage their biometric information directly on their smartphones, avoiding the heavy operational system of centralized servers. Triple encryption allows data storage processing, enabling remote authentication without taking the smartphone from the bag.

GhostPass has confirmed a Proof of Concept (PoC) with a domestic company, CoMax, for use in smart door locks. It will apply in various fields such as security and construction industries, companies in the lobby form, wall pads, mixed-use buildings, hotels, resorts, etc. Furthermore, it can benefit financial and payment solutions by enhancing user convenience and providing secure solutions across diverse industries.

Seon Gwan Lee, the CEO of GhostPass, stated, "We hold a total of 33 patents, including global patents, and have the right to exercise a monopoly within the scope of those patents." He further mentioned, "Even if 6 billion people simultaneously request authentication, the method we use, with 6 billion smart devices serving as servers, ensures scalability is very easy."

CES, the world's largest IT exhibition organized by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), takes place every January in Las Vegas, Nevada. It provides a comprehensive overview of global consumer electronics trends. The convention will run until January 12th.
